### REQ-010: main.cpp integration

- **Status:** DONE
- **Added:** 2026-04-07
- **Completed:** 2026-04-08
- **Verified by:** idf.py build clean (Rev B default config) 2026-04-08
- **Depends on:** REQ-009
- **Description:**

Refactor `espidf/main/main.cpp` to use the Thermo class as the top-level application object. Replace the current flat architecture (global PID, global actuator set, inline MQTT handling, inline status reporting) with Thermo-managed rooms.

#### Current state

`main.cpp` currently:
- Creates global `PidController*` and `ActuatorSet*`
- Has a flat `mqttMessageCallback()` that handles OTA commands inline
- Has a flat `statusReportCallback()` that builds JSON inline
- Control/sensor/UI tasks access singletons directly
- Uses a global `deviceId` string

#### Target state

`main.cpp` becomes a thin orchestrator:

1. **`initSystem()`** — initialize NVS, I2C, sensors, WiFi, MQTT, LittleFS. Create `WhoAmI`. Create `MqttRouter`. Create `Thermo` (which loads config and creates rooms).
2. **`controlTask()`** — calls `thermo->updateControl()` at 100ms (PID + actuators + message queue for all rooms).
3. **`sensorTask()`** — reads sensor hardware at 1s, calls `thermo->updateSensors()` to distribute values.
4. **`uiTask()`** — calls `thermo->updateUi()` at 50ms (encoder/display via the room that owns UI).
5. **`statusReportCallback()`** — calls `thermo->sendStatus()` at 60s.
6. **`app_main()`** — calls `initSystem()`, waits for WiFi/MQTT, validates OTA boot, creates tasks, returns.

#### What moves out of main.cpp

| Current location | Moves to |
|------------------|----------|
| Global `PidController*`, `ActuatorSet*` | Owned by Room instances |
| `mqttMessageCallback()` OTA handling | `Thermo::ProcessJsonAsObj()` |
| `mqttMessageCallback()` set/get dispatch | `MqttRouter` → MessageQueues → `Configurable::ProcessMessage()` |
| `statusReportCallback()` JSON building | `Thermo::GetStatusJsonAsObj()` + `Room::GetStatusJsonAsObj()` |
| `publishDiscovery()` | `Thermo::SendDiscovery()` |
| Global `deviceId` | `WhoAmI::GetDeviceId()` |
| Inline encoder target handling in UI task | `Room::updateUi()` via Ui adapter |

#### What stays in main.cpp

- FreeRTOS task creation and priority assignment
- System-level initialization (NVS, I2C bus, sensor driver init)
- WiFi/MQTT connection sequence with event group waits
- OTA boot validation (one-time check at startup)

#### Stubs directory

After integration, `espidf/main/stubs/` can be removed entirely. All stub implementations are replaced by real code.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [x] `main.cpp` instantiates `WhoAmI`, `MqttRouter`, `Thermo` — no global PID or actuator objects
  - [x] Control task calls `thermo->updateControl()` — PID and actuators managed per-room
  - [x] Sensor task reads hardware and calls `thermo->updateSensors()`
  - [x] UI task calls `thermo->updateUi()` — display driven by Room's Ui adapter
  - [x] Status timer calls `thermo->sendStatus()`
  - [x] MQTT messages routed through `MqttRouter` to correct Room/Thermo queues
  - [ ] First boot without config: discovery sent, install screen shown, device awaits provisioning
  - [ ] Boot with config: rooms created per config, operation screen shown, PID controlling
  - [ ] Room provisioning via MQTT `set` command works end-to-end (server sends config → rooms created → config saved → device operational)
  - [ ] OTA update command still works (routed through Thermo)
  - [ ] Factory reset command works (config deleted, device reboots to first-boot state)
  - [ ] All three hardware variants build (Rev A, Rev B, Special V1)
  - [x] Stubs directory removed
  - [x] Project builds cleanly for all hardware configurations
- **Notes:**
  This is the final integration step. It should be done only after all preceding requirements are complete and individually verified. Test on real hardware with a full provisioning cycle: first boot → MQTT discovery → server sends room config → device configures rooms → PID controls temperature → status reports flow.
